segments.text: The same supreme dhama is simultaneously the highest abode and it is thus suprakasha.
Shankaracharya notes both meanings.
That is the place as well as the radiance.
The paramam dhama is therefore the self-luminous suyam prakasha abode, not a loka somewhere, the cosmos, but within the chit prakasha, light of consciousness.
That is its own stana, station.
It is not a location to reside.
It is the light that makes all locations visible.
That is the paramam, the supreme, the highest.
The dhama, it is not the brahma loka, nor the vaikunta, nor the kailasha of all the loka dhamas.
Within the avyakta, vyakta saikyam.
Whereas the paramam dhama is kala dhita, loka dhita and maya dhita.
That is beyond time, beyond all space and beyond maya.
And why did Krishna say mama?
Krishna, when he says mine, he is talking from that bhava.
Sobhava or swaroopa.
Krishna is identifying the avyakta aksharamam paramam gati as his own supreme abode or mama parama dhamam, my supreme abode.
The maam is simultaneously possessive in the sense that that is Krishna's station, his abode.
That all sadhanas of the chapter were directed towards Krishna.
Krishna's own swaroopa.
When he identifies that, it becomes Krishna's supreme akshara brahman.
Avyakta vyakta sanathanah.
Meaning Krishna is the akshara brahman.
The chapter that began with Arjuna asking him, kim tad brahma, is now ending saying that tad dhama paramam mama.
That, this akshara.
This avyakta, this paramagati is my abode.
My swaroopa.
And here there is an invitation hidden in his say that.
Na punar na nivartande tad dhama paramam mama.
Calling it as mama dhama, Krishna converts the abstract moksha tattva into a personal invitation to a sadhaka.
Come to my abode.
You will never return.
This is the bhakti dimension of Advaithic teaching.
A jnani who recognizes aham brahmasmi and the bhakta who attains Krishna and his supreme abode are arriving at the same destination.
Non-different in the paramartha tattva.
Even if approached through different sampradayas or sadhana.
Sankaracharya says,
tad dhama paramam mama, madhiyam paramam dhama, mat swaroopam eva, paramam brahma.
That param dhama is mine, my own station, which is nothing other than my swaroopa, which is the parabrahman itself.
The equation, tad dhama paramam mama, mama swaroopam, param brahma, krishna's param brahma, is not a loka or krishna inhibits, but a loka.

It is krishna's own swaroopa, which is the paramam brahman, which is akshara, which is also abhyakta, which he mentioned that adi yajnam atradehe, which is the witness present in all of us as the knower of everything.
The entire swaroopa.
The circle of chapter 8 is completed here, with krishna declaring his identity with nirguna brahman.
